  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The stale-head guard lets a differing live head proceed when it is an ancestor of the judged head (`git merge-base --is-ancestor`). The issue says to skip whenever a valid live SHA differs from the judged SHA. A force-push back to an earlier commit during the judge call is therefore not caught, and `close_and_reissue` keeps the judged SHA as its baseline (line 3040).
  WHY: The ancestry check cannot tell the run's own unpushed local commits from a concurrent force-push to an ancestor, so the judge can act on a head that is no longer on the PR. Severity disagreement: anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 rated it NIT with confidence 2, saying the exemption is needed because the judge runs before the push step, and the others rated it MAJOR. The highest severity is kept.

- scripts/review_rb_judge.sh:1929-1933 | severity=NIT | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The `git merge-base --is-ancestor "${RB_LIVE_HEAD_SHA}" "${RB_JUDGED_HEAD_SHA_LC}"` exemption lets a live head that is an ancestor of the judged head proceed. This is narrower than the issue's "differs means skip", so a force-push back to an older commit during the judge run is not caught.
  WHY: The reviewer calls the exemption needed, because the judge runs before the push step and a run with its own unpushed commits always has a live head behind the judged head. A force-push back needs a deliberate human action inside the judge window. The reviewer found no concrete failure beyond this accepted tradeoff.
